newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says still too many abusing asylum system.
newsitem.headline: Germany says still too many abusing asylum system.

text.p: Interior Minister Manfred Kanther said on Wednesday too many foreigners were still abusing the German asylum system to try to gain entry to the country illegally.

"The proportion of those granted asylum of just 7.4 percent in 1996 shows that the large majority are illegal immigrants abusing the right to asylum," Kanther said in a speech to the Federal Office for the Recognition of Foreign Refugees.
Asylum requests have fallen sharply since 1993 when the German government tightened what were previously Europe's most liberal asylum laws to stop an influx of refugees.

But Kanther said new measures, including sending illegal immigrants home more quickly and setting up a computer photo-bank to identify those who repeatedly tried to enter the country, were necessary to stop the abuse of the system.
"We should not be satisfied with the current situation," Kanther said.
The number of foreigners seeking asylum fell to its lowest level in the six-year history of unified Germany last year, down nine percent at 116,397.
Kanther said Germany took in 60 percent of all asylum seekers in the European Union and said the other EU nations should take on more of the burden.
